nodes.scope: Implements Self-Service Portal (delivers the Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant: Patient-support assistant Q&A and 3 related functions use case). Requirements: BR_02, FR_09.

sourceRefs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant: Patient-support assistant Q&A and 3 related functions

sourceRefs.quote: BR4. Every clinical or coverage decision must remain with a licensed staff member; the assistant must never make an autonomous clinical or eligibility determination.
sourceRefs.title: Clinical decisions stay with licensed staff

sourceRefs.quote: FR5. The patient-support assistant must answer common questions about appointment preparation, clinic locations, hours and accepted insurance plans.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-support assistant Q&A

sourceRefs.quote: FR6. The patient-support assistant must retrieve answers from our approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content

sourceRefs.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.
sourceRefs.title: Escalation for clinical-judgement questions

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant availability through the patient portal and public website

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.
sourceRefs.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.
sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Approved-content-only assistant knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: DATA3. Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Six-year document and conversation retention

sourceRefs.quote: DATA5. Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.
sourceRefs.title: Separated encryption for documents and sessions

sourceRefs.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.
sourceRefs.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute

sourceRefs.quote: TECH1. Our infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and would prefer the new intake and assistant platform to run on AWS.
sourceRefs.title: AWS as target cloud platform

sourceRefs.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant

sourceRefs.quote: CON1. We would like a phased rollout starting with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.
sourceRefs.title: 24-week phased rollout starting with intake

sourceRefs.quote: CON3. Our compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.
sourceRefs.title: Compliance sign-off before any patient-facing pilot

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Patient Portal

sourceRefs.quote: Our clinics see approximately 85,000 patient encounters per month across primary care, behavioural health and physical therapy.
sourceRefs.title: Patient

sourceRefs.quote: The Director of Patient Access asked whether the assistant could eventually support Spanish-language conversations, given about 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but this was not committed to for the initial phase.
sourceRefs.title: Spanish-language coverage gap at launch

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant deployment form undecided

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Policy documents are reusable for a knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Should the assistant be standalone or embedded in the portal?

sourceRefs.quote: BR2. The solution must reduce routine front-desk call volume by giving patients a self-service way to get appointment-prep and billing answers.
sourceRefs.title: Reduce routine front-desk call volume

sourceRefs.title: Patient-support assistant Q&A

sourceRefs.quote: FR6. The patient-support assistant must retrieve answers from our approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content

sourceRefs.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.
sourceRefs.title: Escalation for clinical-judgement questions

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant availability through the patient portal and public website

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.
sourceRefs.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.
sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.

sourceRefs.quote: DATA3. Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Six-year document and conversation retention

sourceRefs.quote: DATA5. Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.
sourceRefs.title: Separated encryption for documents and sessions

sourceRefs.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.
sourceRefs.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute

sourceRefs.quote: TECH1. Our infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and would prefer the new intake and assistant platform to run on AWS.

sourceRefs.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant

sourceRefs.quote: CON1. We would like a phased rollout starting with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.
sourceRefs.title: 24-week phased rollout starting with intake

sourceRefs.quote: CON3. Our compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.
sourceRefs.title: Compliance sign-off before any patient-facing pilot

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.

sourceRefs.quote: Our clinics see approximately 85,000 patient encounters per month across primary care, behavioural health and physical therapy.

sourceRefs.quote: The Director of Patient Access asked whether the assistant could eventually support Spanish-language conversations, given about 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but this was not committed to for the initial phase.
sourceRefs.title: Spanish-language coverage gap at launch

sourceRefs.title: Should the assistant be standalone or embedded in the portal?

sourceRefs.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content

sourceRefs.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.

nodes.scope: Implements Core Platform Services (delivers the Document extraction pipeline with human validation: Structured field extraction and 1 related function use case). Requirements: NFR_01, NFR_02, NFR_03, NFR_04, NFR_05, NFR_06, INT_02, INT_03, INT_04, DATA_04, SEC_01, SEC_05, SEC_06.

sourceRefs.title: Document extraction pipeline with human validation: Structured field extraction and 1 related function

sourceRefs.quote: FR2. The system must extract structured fields from each document, including patient identifiers, referring provider, requested service and supporting clinical notes.
sourceRefs.title: Structured field extraction

sourceRefs.quote: FR10. The system should flag documents where extraction confidence is low so clerks review those first.
sourceRefs.title: Low-confidence extraction flagging for clerk review

sourceRefs.quote: NFR2. Document extraction results must be available to a reviewing clerk within 5 minutes of document receipt for 95% of documents.
sourceRefs.title: 5-minute extraction turnaround

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant

sourceRefs.quote: CON2. The medical records team must be able to fall back to today's manual process at any time during the initial rollout if extraction quality is not trusted yet.
sourceRefs.title: Fallback to today's manual process during rollout

sourceRefs.quote: Referral letters, prior-authorisation forms and outside lab results arrive by fax, secure email and patient portal upload, and today a team of eleven medical records clerks manually reads and keys each document into our EHR.
sourceRefs.title: Extraction-accuracy risk across document sources

sourceRefs.quote: NFR1. The intake system must process at least 85,000 patient encounters worth of associated documents per month without a growing backlog.
sourceRefs.title: 85,000 patient encounters per month at scale

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.
sourceRefs.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations

sourceRefs.quote: NFR5. The system must maintain 99.5% availability during clinic operating hours, 7am to 8pm Pacific, seven days a week.
sourceRefs.title: 99.5% availability during clinic hours

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT2. The intake system must accept inbound documents from our existing fax gateway, secure email inbox and patient-portal upload mechanism.
sourceRefs.title: Inbound document channel integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.
sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA4. Conversation logs must be reviewable by compliance staff but must not be used to retrain or fine-tune any model without a separate, explicit approval process.
sourceRefs.title: Conversation-log governance for model training

sourceRefs.quote: SEC1. The solution must comply with HIPAA, including a signed business associate agreement with any AI provider or subprocessor involved.
sourceRefs.title: HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA

sourceRefs.quote: SEC5. The solution must undergo a HIPAA security risk assessment before go-live.
sourceRefs.title: HIPAA security risk assessment before go-live

sourceRefs.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.
sourceRefs.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.

sourceRefs.quote: NFR5. The system must maintain 99.5% availability during clinic operating hours, 7am to 8pm Pacific, seven days a week.
sourceRefs.title: 99.5% availability during clinic hours

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT2. The intake system must accept inbound documents from our existing fax gateway, secure email inbox and patient-portal upload mechanism.

sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA4. Conversation logs must be reviewable by compliance staff but must not be used to retrain or fine-tune any model without a separate, explicit approval process.
sourceRefs.title: Conversation-log governance for model training

sourceRefs.quote: SEC1. The solution must comply with HIPAA, including a signed business associate agreement with any AI provider or subprocessor involved.
sourceRefs.title: HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA

sourceRefs.title: HIPAA security risk assessment before go-live

sourceRefs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant: Patient-support assistant Q&A and 3 related functions

sourceRefs.quote: BR4. Every clinical or coverage decision must remain with a licensed staff member; the assistant must never make an autonomous clinical or eligibility determination.
sourceRefs.title: Clinical decisions stay with licensed staff

sourceRefs.quote: FR5. The patient-support assistant must answer common questions about appointment preparation, clinic locations, hours and accepted insurance plans.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-support assistant Q&A

sourceRefs.quote: FR6. The patient-support assistant must retrieve answers from our approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content

sourceRefs.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.
sourceRefs.title: Escalation for clinical-judgement questions

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant availability through the patient portal and public website

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.
sourceRefs.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.
sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Approved-content-only assistant knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: DATA3. Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Six-year document and conversation retention

sourceRefs.quote: DATA5. Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.
sourceRefs.title: Separated encryption for documents and sessions

sourceRefs.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.
sourceRefs.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute

sourceRefs.quote: TECH1. Our infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and would prefer the new intake and assistant platform to run on AWS.
sourceRefs.title: AWS as target cloud platform

sourceRefs.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant

sourceRefs.quote: CON1. We would like a phased rollout starting with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.
sourceRefs.title: 24-week phased rollout starting with intake

sourceRefs.quote: CON3. Our compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.
sourceRefs.title: Compliance sign-off before any patient-facing pilot

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Patient Portal

sourceRefs.quote: Our clinics see approximately 85,000 patient encounters per month across primary care, behavioural health and physical therapy.
sourceRefs.title: Patient

sourceRefs.quote: The Director of Patient Access asked whether the assistant could eventually support Spanish-language conversations, given about 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but this was not committed to for the initial phase.
sourceRefs.title: Spanish-language coverage gap at launch

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant deployment form undecided

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Policy documents are reusable for a knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Should the assistant be standalone or embedded in the portal?

sourceRefs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant: Patient-support assistant Q&A and 3 related functions

sourceRefs.quote: BR4. Every clinical or coverage decision must remain with a licensed staff member; the assistant must never make an autonomous clinical or eligibility determination.
sourceRefs.title: Clinical decisions stay with licensed staff

sourceRefs.quote: FR5. The patient-support assistant must answer common questions about appointment preparation, clinic locations, hours and accepted insurance plans.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-support assistant Q&A

sourceRefs.quote: FR6. The patient-support assistant must retrieve answers from our approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content

sourceRefs.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.
sourceRefs.title: Escalation for clinical-judgement questions

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant availability through the patient portal and public website

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.
sourceRefs.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.
sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Approved-content-only assistant knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: DATA3. Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Six-year document and conversation retention

sourceRefs.quote: DATA5. Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.
sourceRefs.title: Separated encryption for documents and sessions

sourceRefs.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.
sourceRefs.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute

sourceRefs.quote: TECH1. Our infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and would prefer the new intake and assistant platform to run on AWS.
sourceRefs.title: AWS as target cloud platform

sourceRefs.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant

sourceRefs.quote: CON1. We would like a phased rollout starting with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.
sourceRefs.title: 24-week phased rollout starting with intake

sourceRefs.quote: CON3. Our compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.
sourceRefs.title: Compliance sign-off before any patient-facing pilot

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Patient Portal

sourceRefs.quote: Our clinics see approximately 85,000 patient encounters per month across primary care, behavioural health and physical therapy.
sourceRefs.title: Patient

sourceRefs.quote: The Director of Patient Access asked whether the assistant could eventually support Spanish-language conversations, given about 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but this was not committed to for the initial phase.
sourceRefs.title: Spanish-language coverage gap at launch

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant deployment form undecided

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Policy documents are reusable for a knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Should the assistant be standalone or embedded in the portal?

nodes.scope: Implements AI Conversational Assistant (delivers the Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant: Patient-support assistant Q&A and 3 related functions use case). Requirements: BR_04, FR_05, FR_06, FR_09.

sourceRefs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant: Patient-support assistant Q&A and 3 related functions

sourceRefs.quote: BR4. Every clinical or coverage decision must remain with a licensed staff member; the assistant must never make an autonomous clinical or eligibility determination.
sourceRefs.title: Clinical decisions stay with licensed staff

sourceRefs.quote: FR5. The patient-support assistant must answer common questions about appointment preparation, clinic locations, hours and accepted insurance plans.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-support assistant Q&A

sourceRefs.quote: FR6. The patient-support assistant must retrieve answers from our approved clinic policy and FAQ documents rather than generating unsourced medical guidance.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant answers grounded in approved policy content

sourceRefs.quote: FR7. The patient-support assistant must recognise when a question requires clinical judgement or involves symptoms and must hand off to a human staff member.
sourceRefs.title: Escalation for clinical-judgement questions

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant availability through the patient portal and public website

sourceRefs.quote: NFR3. The solution must support approximately 1,200 clinical and administrative staff users plus patient-facing assistant traffic estimated at 85,000 conversations per month.
sourceRefs.title: 1,200 staff plus 85,000 monthly conversations

sourceRefs.quote: NFR6. Every assistant answer and every extracted field must be traceable back to the source document or policy document it came from.
sourceRefs.title: Traceable extraction and assistant answers

sourceRefs.quote: NFR4. The patient-support assistant must respond to a typical question within 4 seconds.
sourceRefs.title: 4-second assistant response time

sourceRefs.quote: INT3. The patient-support assistant should integrate with Five9 so a handed-off conversation can be routed to an available front-desk agent with context preserved.
sourceRefs.title: Five9 handoff integration

sourceRefs.quote: INT4. The assistant must authenticate patients through the existing patient-portal login rather than introducing a separate identity system.
sourceRefs.title: Patient-portal authentication reuse

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Approved-content-only assistant knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: DATA3. Extracted document data and assistant conversation logs must be retained for at least six years to satisfy state medical-records requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Six-year document and conversation retention

sourceRefs.quote: DATA5. Document images and extracted text must be encrypted at rest, separate from the assistant's conversational session data.
sourceRefs.title: Separated encryption for documents and sessions

sourceRefs.quote: SEC6. The patient-support assistant must never display another patient's information, even if a conversation is misrouted.
sourceRefs.title: No cross-patient information disclosure on misroute

sourceRefs.quote: TECH1. Our infrastructure team runs existing workloads on Amazon Web Services and would prefer the new intake and assistant platform to run on AWS.
sourceRefs.title: AWS as target cloud platform

sourceRefs.quote: TECH2. We are open to a managed AI/ML service for document extraction and the assistant, as long as it can meet our HIPAA and data-handling requirements.
sourceRefs.title: Managed AI/ML service for extraction and assistant

sourceRefs.quote: CON1. We would like a phased rollout starting with document intake within 24 weeks of contract signature, with the patient-support assistant following in a second phase.
sourceRefs.title: 24-week phased rollout starting with intake

sourceRefs.quote: CON3. Our compliance officer must approve the assistant's response content and escalation rules before any patient-facing pilot begins.
sourceRefs.title: Compliance sign-off before any patient-facing pilot

sourceRefs.quote: FR8. The assistant must be available through our existing patient portal and, if feasible, as a widget on our public website.
sourceRefs.title: Patient Portal

sourceRefs.quote: Our clinics see approximately 85,000 patient encounters per month across primary care, behavioural health and physical therapy.
sourceRefs.title: Patient

sourceRefs.quote: The Director of Patient Access asked whether the assistant could eventually support Spanish-language conversations, given about 18% of patients prefer Spanish, but this was not committed to for the initial phase.
sourceRefs.title: Spanish-language coverage gap at launch

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Assistant deployment form undecided

sourceRefs.quote: DATA2. The assistant's knowledge base must be built only from clinic-approved policy, FAQ and appointment-prep documents, refreshed whenever those documents change.
sourceRefs.title: Policy documents are reusable for a knowledge base

sourceRefs.quote: No decision has been made yet on whether the assistant runs as a fully separate application or is embedded directly inside the existing patient portal.
sourceRefs.title: Should the assistant be standalone or embedded in the portal?
